subject: Function definitions, fallback matrix & PoC access — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike@elarahealth.com>, Priya Das <priya.das@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Function definitions, fallback matrix & PoC access — next steps

Hi Mike + Priya,

Great conversation this morning — thanks for walking us through your clinician workflow and the constraints around latency and PHI handling. Per request, I captured the technical asks and proposed next steps below so we can align on the PoC scope. I kept this focused on integration/architecture items we discussed: SDK setup, auth, routing, structured output (function calling), embeddings/rerankers, and failure/fallback behavior.

Quick TL;DR (ask + our proposal):
- PoC access: short-lived API key + VPC peering for log review (Elara to sign off) — Redwood to create sandbox project.
- SDK: use Redwood Node SDK (v1.4) with service-account style key rotation; sample config in Drive link.
- Auth: primary = API key scoped to PoC; optional = mTLS for SRE — we can enable if you want host-based mutual auth.
- Routing: per-route policy — low-latency path (small model) for triage, high-quality path (larger model) for summary/rerank; automatic fallback to cheaper model on capacity alarms.
- Function calling: we recommend explicit function schemas (JSON schema) for: patient_summary, medication_extraction, followup_action. Include strict type constraints for PHI redaction flag.
- Embeddings & reranker: local embeddings store (Elara-owned vector DB) plus Redwood-hosted reranker endpoint that takes top-K candidates.
- Error handling: parallel tool calls where helpful, but canonicalize errors upstream; fallback matrix attached (fn-fallback-matrix.csv).

Action items / proposed mutual action plan (dates):
1) Elara: Share PoC sign-off + SRE contact by Wed 2028-07-27.
2) Redwood: Provision sandbox project + API key, upload SDK quickstart + example function defs by Fri 2028-07-28.
3) Joint: 60-min engineering sync to wire SDK + run initial end-to-end by Tue 2028-08-01.

Notes on the function schema approach (short):
- Define functions as explicit JSON schemas (not freeform). This lets Redwood validate outputs and trigger rerank/embeddings steps deterministically.
- Keep function outputs small and strongly typed — avoid nested free text where possible.
- For long-running tool calls (e.g., EMR lookups) use async callbacks + job_id in function response; Redwood can surface job status in streaming responses.

Auth & SDK configuration (practical):
- Use the Node SDK with the following settings in PoC:
  - apiKey: short-lived scoped key (PoC-only)
  - enableAutoRetry: true (SDK-level exponential backoff)
  - routePolicy: "latency-first" for triage endpoints, "quality-first" for summarizers
  - kvCache: disabled in PoC unless you want to test prefix caching (we can enable)

Attachments: I attached a concise cheatsheet (redwood-sdk-auth-cheatsheet.pdf) and a draft fallback matrix (fn-fallback-matrix.csv).

If that looks good I’ll provision the sandbox and send the API key + onboarding notes. Also happy to spin up a quick demo of the function definitions and parallel tool call pattern if you want code-first examples during the engineering sync.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mike Chen <mike@elarahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Function definitions, fallback matrix & PoC access

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before we sign off on PoC access: 

1) PHI handling: Our compliance team requires that any model output marked as PHI be written back to our audit log and that the model never persist full EMR text outside our vector DB. Can you confirm Redwood will not store model inputs in the hosted reranker?
2) mTLS: Our SRE would prefer mTLS for the initial PoC; they’ll provide certs if Redwood can accept them on the sandbox host.
3) Embedding pipeline: We plan to host embeddings in our Pinecone cluster — will Redwood reranker call to our cluster, or do you need us to replicate vectors into a Redwood-managed cache?

Also, provisional ok on the 8/1 sync — can we shift to 8/2 afternoon PST if that helps your provisioning timeline?

- Mike
Mike Chen
Head of Product, Elara Health
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike@elarahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Priya Das <priya.das@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Function definitions, fallback matrix & PoC access

On Tue, Jul 25, 2028 at 10:05 AM Mike Chen <mike@elarahealth.com> wrote:
> 1) PHI handling: Our compliance team requires that any model output marked as PHI be written back to our audit log and that the model never persist full EMR text outside our vector DB. Can you confirm Redwood will not store model inputs in the hosted reranker?

Hi Mike — good questions. Short answers: yes and a path forward.

- Storage: For the PoC we will not retain full inputs on the Redwood-hosted reranker. We support an option where only tokenized embeddings or hashed metadata are processed by Redwood and raw EMR text remains in Elara's environment. We will document audit logging hooks so outputs flagged PHI are mirrored to your audit endpoint.

- mTLS: We can accept client certs on the sandbox endpoint. Please share the certs in our SFTP; we’ll configure the sandbox load balancer to require client cert authentication.

- Embeddings: We support both approaches: (a) Redwood calling your Pinecone cluster over private peering (recommended for data locality), or (b) replicating a shallow index into Redwood-managed cache for latency-sensitive reranking. For the PoC, option (a) is simplest and avoids replication.

Implementation notes on function-calling & parallel tool strategy:
- Tool definitions: keep 3–5 canonical functions per user flow. Example: patient_summary(schema), med_entities(list), next_steps(action_items).
- Parallel calls: For search/rerank we recommend triggering the vector search + an immediate lightweight heuristic filter in parallel to reduce tail latency; then fan-in results into the reranker. The reranker should accept a candidate list and return a ranked top-3 with confidence scores.
- Error handling: if a backend call fails, return a typed error object in the function response (e.g., {error_type: "backend_unavailable", retryable: true, code: 503}) so the calling app can decide to show a cached summary or surface a degraded message.
- Fallback model: Use model-light for latency-sensitive triage with a 150ms SLO, fall back to model-high for accuracy when SLO allows; see attached fallback matrix for thresholds.

I'll draft the minimal function JSON schemas and drop them into the Drive link by EOD. Jordan — can you provision the sandbox and request SRE cert upload?

Thanks,
Sean

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

If anything changes on timelines I’ll update the HubSpot deal and the Drive folder. Looking forward to the PoC — we’ll keep the first run to a small clinician subset as discussed.

Best,
Jordan
